summary.headline: Ashiana Housing FY26 booking value hit record Rs 2,421 crore (+25% YoY); Q4 bookings Rs 1,290 crore driven by Gurugram Aaroham launch.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 bookings of Rs 1,290 crore rose 124% YoY, led by Ashiana Aaroham Phase-I and II in Gurugram (about Rs 833 crore at launch), with realisation up 71% YoY to Rs 11,566 per sq ft. Q4 total income rose 46% YoY to Rs 335 crore on handovers in Jaipur, Pune and Chennai, while PAT was flat at Rs 21 crore (6.26% margin). For FY26, total income more than doubled to Rs 1,187 crore, EBITDA rose 281% to Rs 176 crore (14.85% margin) and PAT reached Rs 118 crore versus Rs 18 crore in FY25. Management added about 2.9 lakh sq ft-equivalent of Senior Living land and reiterated a Rs 2,200 crore FY27 pre-sales target.

segments.name: Senior Living
segments.commentary: FY26 bookings Rs 570 crore (+55% YoY); management targets over Rs 700 crore in FY27. Five projects with GDV over Rs 6,500 crore to launch in 12-24 months across Chennai, Bangalore and Bombay-Pune.

segments.name: Residential (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi, Pune, Chennai, Jamshedpur)
segments.commentary: Q4 bookings driven by Gurugram Aaroham Phase-I/II (about Rs 833 crore at launch). Jaipur and Jamshedpur realisations now above Rs 7,000 per sq ft; management flagged early oversupply signs in Gurugram and Pune.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales target of Rs 2,200 crore, with Senior Living target above Rs 700 crore.

Launches planned in FY27: Ashiana Oma (Jaipur, about 10 acres, Rs 7,500-8,000 per sq ft, within a couple of months), Ashiana Aaranya and Tattvam (Q4 FY27), Aaroham Phase-III, and at least one phase in each Senior Living project.
Margin outlook: FY27 full-year margin to be better than FY26 and FY28 better than FY27, with quarterly volatility; Malhar Phase-II and Anmol Phase-III are low-margin.
Reported ROE of above 20% targeted for FY27; FY30 cumulative PAT guidance of Rs 2,000 crore reiterated as on track.
Blended realisation expected to move in a Rs 9,000-11,000 per sq ft range, with about Rs 10,000 as a near-term aim.
Construction cost inflation expected at 8-10% YoY in FY27; no inflation underwritten at land acquisition.
Capital to be redeployed into growth rather than buybacks or large dividends; Senior Living to receive the bulk of capital.
Senior Living projects targeted at 30-35% project-level margins (35-40% gross, 5-6% selling cost).
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 96 lakh sq ft post recent additions (about 4x annual throughput); management says more land must be added this year.

Acquired 8.83 acres in Raigad for about Rs 450 crore sales potential; Panvel (agreement, about Rs 1,000 crore); Vadgaon (28.5 acres, about 20 lakh sq ft, Rs 1,800-2,000 crore GDV); Bangalore (about 11 lakh sq ft, CP resolution pending, about 2 months).
Phases totalling about 25 lakh sq ft to be launched by FY31 across Vatsalya, Advik, Swarang and Aaroham.
Delivery timing: Oma phase by FY30; Aaranya and Tattvam partly FY31; Wavarle, Vadgaon and Bangalore launched in FY28 with FY30-31 deliveries.
Mahindra World City Jaipur lease terminated after 18 months without approvals; Aaranya (22.7 acres, Chennai) is a separate, ongoing project.
demand_pricing: Gurugram: signs of oversupply, with unsold inventory up for two consecutive quarters after heavy launches; management says sustained trend for about four more quarters would cause oversupply.
Pune: early oversupply signs; Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur and Jaipur show no oversupply yet.
Senior Living sales are mostly direct (about 40% Bombay, 40% Pune and 20% rest of India/NRI at Amodh); channel partner use is limited.
Amodh newer phases at about Rs 8,200-8,300 per sq ft; Amodh Phase-III around Rs 8,500 per sq ft used as the Vadgaon benchmark.
Competition in Senior Living seen as market-expanding; few peers building large (12-15 acre) projects with comparable amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Mahindra World City (Jaipur) lease terminated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the counterparty could not obtain social infrastructure approvals after about 18 months, so the transaction could not proceed; the lease was terminated, with scope to restart later.

qa_highlights.question: Project-level margin and cost breakup for Senior Living?
qa_highlights.answer: Project margins are expected at 30-35%; gross margin 35-40%, selling cost 5-6%. Land is 10-20% and hard construction 40-50% of revenue, with soft costs about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Construction cost inflation assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: No inflation underwritten at land purchase; management expects 8-10% construction cost increase in FY27 YoY on current information.

qa_highlights.question: Is annuity or leasing a major Senior Living revenue stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Not within five years; yields are low and leasing deposit structures are not viable. Home sales remain the main profit source, and assisted living is outsourced partly to Epoch Elder Care (Nirmay, Bhiwadi).

qa_highlights.question: Is there oversupply in the markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No oversupply yet overall. Gurugram and Pune show early signs; Jaipur, Jamshedpur and Bhiwadi show none.

qa_highlights.question: What is the class action suit status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has moved the Delhi High Court against class action applicability; a ruling is hoped for within FY27, but consumer complaints will continue for the filers regardless.

risks_watch: Construction cost inflation (8-10% expected in FY27) and labour and material shortages affecting delivery timelines.
Low-margin projects Malhar Phase-II and Anmol Phase-III may dent quarterly margins; FY27 ROE above 20% has little room for slippage.
Oversupply signs in Gurugram and Pune, which carry large inventory.
Class action litigation over an older Kolkata/Pune-area project (Project Maitri-related disputes settled separately); outcome timing uncertain.
Execution of Bangalore land (CP still pending) and Panvel pricing not yet fixed; Maharashtra senior living policy not yet notified.
Management flagged that a sustained rise in unsold inventory in Gurugram would signal oversupply.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Senior Living growth and FY30 targets, but guarded on macro and geopolitical impact, and evasive on project-level pricing and investment detail. Cautious on Gurugram and Pune supply, and openly defensive on the class action suit.
key_quotes: We are in the bottom of the top tier of brands in Gurugram. We want to get into a higher tier there for the product we are in.
The profitability in the next five years will continue to come from home sales.
I think we are expecting about 8-10% increase in construction costs in this financial year, on a year-on-year basis, as of now.
There is no oversupply yet. Signs of some oversupply in Gurugram and Pune are visible.

growth.why: Management targets FY27 pre-sales of Rs 2,200 crore (Senior Living above Rs 700 crore) and ROE above 20%, backed by Gurugram Aaroham bookings (~Rs 833 crore at launch), a Rs 96 lakh sq ft land bank (~4x annual throughput) and launches like Oma and Aaranya, but no explicit revenue growth % is guided and Gurugram/Pune show early oversupply.
